learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Apple, 60 cents poorer and locked the result after six preferred swaps under cyclic fruit preferences.
observations.exploration: Ran six swaps: back to cherry, paid 60 cents. Ran three: back to cherry, paid 30. Selected the apple-first ranking: apple after two swaps, paid 20. Pressing six swaps again returned to the cyclic cherry result rather than replaying the ranked mode; the controls act as scenario presets.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to cherry, sixty cents poorer. It accurately quoted the three- and six-swap cycles and the ranked case stopping after two, then explained transitive preferences remove the exploitable circle.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot after six swaps. Three fruit cards formed a directed triangle with ten-cent arrows; a seven-fruit trail returned to cherry and the paid amount read sixty cents. Historical results stayed visible.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884175 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The prompt challenges equating locally preferred moves with global improvement.
prediction.evidence: Selected an improved final item despite a six-step cycle.

interaction.reason: Cycle lengths and a ranked contrast isolate preference consistency.
interaction.evidence: Three and six swaps return to cherry; the ranking reaches apple and stops.

payoff.reason: The reveal explains the observed loss and the role of transitivity.
payoff.evidence: It accurately counts the ranked case's two swaps.

clarity.reason: The graph is clear, but replay instructions are ambiguous about scenario resets.
clarity.evidence: Pressing six swaps after ranking silently restores the cyclic scenario.

transfer.reason: The ending connects the toy to a concrete choice-model assumption and its condition.
transfer.evidence: Transitive ranking prevents a seller repeatedly charging for a cycle of preferred swaps.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Every desired swap can leave the buyer with the same item and less money.
surprise.evidence: Both complete cycles return to cherry after paying.

visualExplanation.reason: The directed triangle and fruit trail make the loop visible.
visualExplanation.evidence: The six-swap trail circles back twice.

playfulness.reason: Fruit swaps make a consistency condition tangible.
playfulness.evidence: Three scenarios show repeated cycles and a terminating ranking.

practicalValue.reason: It illustrates why consistent preference ordering matters.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal ties transitivity to avoiding a money-pump cycle.

depth.reason: The ranked contrast explains the failure rather than only showing it.
depth.evidence: Removing the cycle creates a best item where paid improvements stop.

complexity.reason: The fruit paths are simple, while transitive preference consistency is an abstract condition.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: distinguish pairwise preferred steps from a coherent overall order.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low, with ambiguity from scenario buttons that reset the mode.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: A local preference cycle can permit repeated losses with no net item improvement.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Transitivity and choice models are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Low: directed arrows, fruit sequence and cent totals.

whyCool: A sequence of individually welcome trades can sell someone a round trip back to what they already owned.
caveat: The payment willingness is stipulated and the replay buttons select scenarios rather than preserving a ranked mode.
missingEvidence: Transient swap motion was not separately inspected; final trails and states were inspected.
No fresh preference set was tested.
